title: Branch the onboard verification notice on the skill's existence, not on a missing test command
action:
RED FIRST. Write the failing tests before any production edit, run them, and keep the red output — it is the cap proof's first half.

Today `stale_advisor_notices` in notices.rs decides the verification notice from whether the repo declares a test command. Find it with `rg -n 'else if !has_test' packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/onboard/notices.rs` — one hit, the line reads `    } else if !has_test {`. Above it sits `    if commands.is_some_and(|c| c.contains_key("verify"))`, the retired-key arm. Below, `fn declares_test` is the one definition of 'this repo declares a test command'; find it with `rg -n 'fn declares_test'`.

The existing test that pins today's behavior is `fn a_declared_test_command_draws_no_notice_in_any_shape()` — find it with `rg -n 'a_declared_test_command_draws_no_notice_in_any_shape'`. It asserts a repo with a declared test gets NO notice. Under this cell that repo MUST get one, so this test flips red on its own. Rewrite it to assert the new truth; do not delete it.

What to build, per D3 (65592f3f):

1. The notice now keys off whether this repo HAS a verification skill, read from the SOURCE tree, never from a rendered skill home (plan.md, Decisions taken 1 — a fresh clone before any `--apply` has the source but may have no rendered copy). Per D8 (9f4f90f0) the source path is `.bee/verify/verify-app/SKILL.md`, relative to the repo root already passed into `stale_advisor_notices`.
2. Per D1 (d0e3c3a0), `verify-app` is a CONSTANT, identical in every repo. Add it to templates.rs beside the other constants as a `pub const`, and build the probe path from it. Never write the literal string twice.
3. Skill ABSENT -> a generate notice naming the `bee-verifying` skill. Skill PRESENT -> a new upkeep notice naming the `bee-verify-upkeep` skill. Nothing in the codebase names `bee-verify-upkeep` in a notice today.
4. Per plan.md Decisions taken 4, the generate notice needs TWO wordings, because the existing constant opens 'This project has no command that proves it works' — true for a repo with no test command, FALSE for one that declares tests. A repo with tests still has nothing that drives the real product; say that instead. Keep the existing constant for the no-test case; author a second for the has-test case.
5. Per plan.md Decisions taken 5, the generate notice must not nag. Onboard re-runs on every bee version mismatch and bee tags several releases a day, so the notice text instructs the reading agent to search the decision log for a recorded refusal before offering again. The upkeep notice is a pointer, not a prompt: it names the skill and stops.
6. Per plan.md Decisions taken 3, the upkeep notice is where a composed test command gets REPORTED, never rewritten — but that line belongs to the bee-verify-upkeep skill body in slice 2, not to this cell. Do not edit any skill file here.
7. The retired `commands.verify` arm keeps precedence and its warnings are unchanged. Decide the arm order explicitly and state it in a comment, because the existing comment 'Mutually exclusive BY CONSTRUCTION' describes the OLD order and will be wrong after this change.

Tests, red first, all six states of the truth table (skill absent/present x test declared/absent x legacy verify key present):
  - skill absent + no test command -> the existing generate notice
  - skill absent + test declared -> the second generate notice, and assert its first sentence DIFFERS from the first one
  - skill present + no test command -> the upkeep notice
  - skill present + test declared -> the upkeep notice
  - legacy `commands.verify` key + skill absent -> the retirement warning still wins
  - legacy `commands.verify` key + skill present -> the arm order you chose, asserted, with no double notice

The existing fixture is `fn stale_notices_for` — find it with `rg -n 'fn stale_notices_for'`. It takes config JSON only, so it needs a repo root or a skill-present flag to reach the new states; extend it rather than writing a second fixture.

Also extend the hygiene test `fn the_verification_offer_speaks_to_the_user_without_internal_terms` (find it by name) to cover BOTH new constants. Note its banned list includes the literal `.bee` — so no notice may name the source path. Two more of its assertions matter: a notice names its skill, and the offer stays the user's to accept.

STAY IN RUST. This cell touches exactly the two files in `files`. No skill file, no doc, no config, no `bee dev regen`.

truths: A repo that declares commands.test and has no verification skill now receives a generate notice; before this cell it received none
A repo that has .bee/verify/verify-app/SKILL.md receives an upkeep notice naming bee-verify-upkeep, whether or not it declares a test command
A repo carrying the retired commands.verify key still receives its retirement warning
The two generate notices have different first sentences

artifacts.substantive: a pub const for the verify-app skill name, a second generate-notice constant, and one upkeep-notice constant; no TODO stubs
the branch reads the source skill path; six state tests plus the extended hygiene test, all named and asserting

key_links: notices.rs builds its probe path from the templates.rs verify-app constant, never from a repeated string literal
a_declared_test_command_draws_no_notice_in_any_shape is rewritten to the new truth, not deleted
prohibitions: No file outside the two in files
No literal verify-app string written twice
No notice text containing the string .bee, commands., config.json, gate, cap or proof
The existence check never reads .claude/skills, .agents/skills or .opencode/skills
